content: Between the silent courtroom and the sealed prison van, words have been drained of their colour by years and high walls. Today, as the gavel falls and the verdict is read, language loses its weight before the heavy iron doors. Through fogged car windows and cold railings, the hands of those watching the courtroom proceedings cross in mid-air: some raise a defiant V sign, others wave in vain, while some press their palms together in prayer. On the edge of this silenced city, the once brilliant candlelight has faded, yet what remains are these faint, almost frantic gestures — sketching out the quietest form of resistance. These soundless gestures carve an indelible echo into the air, pale and faint, yet stubbornly suspended in the late-summer breeze. This is both a farewell and memory's final upright spine before suffocation — the last tender cry before the high walls.
